answer: Each identity keeps one distinct pre-1980 mechanical watch, its serial entered in a public atlas and a unique pigment dot sealed on its dial. Monthly, verifiers name a random time; the holder films setting the watch to it on its vault island plinth while a microphone records the movement's beat-error fingerprint, matched to enrolment. Copied video fails the random time, shared watch fails the fingerprint. 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 movements at $210 each plus $80 yearly servicing, and lose a 5-coin bond per missed or cloned check; trade-off: repairers are scarce, so admission is slow.
